original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

actual_scope: For two same-input calls that each add twice the same rank-8 scalar child f into separate dirty targets D1 and D2, test whether the child result can be shared through the existing D1 target: repeat NEG(D1), ADD(D2,D1), NEG(D1), child_plus(D1), ADD(D2,D1) twice. The proposed map is (D1,D2)->(D1+2f,D2+2f), with D1,D2 arbitrary and no extra temporary.
scope_change_reason: Refined the card to an explicit two-output dirty-target wrapper because the broad boundary question had no supplier-specific restoration instance established within this bounded cycle. The new scope tests a concrete local mechanism that removes two of four same-input rank-eight child invocations under a named additive child contract, while leaving supplier adoption as an open follow-up.
selection_rationale: The coverage-law suggestion overlaps the live plane-port claim in Discussion 1587; the connector-alphabet suggestion overlaps the completed DUO extension in PR 1531; the centre-sharing suggestion overlaps the adjacent-call center-register question and selected-stage findings in Discussion 1516 and PRs 1664/1684. This is a distinct persistent-boundary construction: reuse one recursive child output across two dirty accumulators, changing the child-call profile rather than only the frame schedule.

bottleneck_link: If admitted to the complex supplier, sharing this output would replace four rank-8 child calls by two per paired output, reducing the binding-side child moment; the extra scalar target gates and the changed two-output contract are priced separately.
stop_rule: Only the rank-8 length-eight dot-product child, two arbitrary dirty scalar targets, and two consecutive same-input outputs are in scope. Stop if the exact dirty map fails, if the required additive child contract is unavailable, or if the fully charged moment with the scalar gates is not below two separate calls. Do not infer supplier admission from this pilot.
evidence: Exact symbolic affine execution proves (D1,D2)->(D1+2f,D2+2f) for arbitrary integer dirty targets and child value. Positive fixture covers all 65,536 Boolean source pairs with all 9 target pairs (589,824 combined cases); controls omitting the restoring NEG and final ADD both reject the witness (2,5,3). Invoice: baseline 4 rank-8 calls; candidate 2 rank-8 calls plus 4 ADD and 4 NEG gates, no extra temporary. Using exact outward rational enclosures at selected a=67018507072324140917/40000000000000000000000 and charging each gate one phi_1 unit, candidate upper 0.3303711890451098 < baseline lower 0.4399830566696027 (at least 24.9127% lower in this surrogate screen). The source/frame schedule is held fixed. This is a local mechanism only: the selected supplier's dirty-child interface, transfer bill, tape and precision admission are not established; the endpoint is not a new kappa.
